tldr: UItron is an open-source foundational GUI agent model that achieves superior performance in GUI perception, grounding, and planning through systematic data engineering, a unified interactive infrastructure, and a curriculum reinforcement learning framework, with particular strength in Chinese app scenarios.
contributions: Systematic investigation of data engineering strategies (data unification, trajectory distillation, manual annotation) and interactive infrastructure for GUI agents
Curriculum Reinforcement Learning (CuRL) framework with group relative policy optimization using dense offline rewards and credible online rewards
Open-sourced UItron achieving superior performance in GUI perception, grounding, and offline planning benchmarks with competitive results in online agent environments

Significant improvement in Chinese scenario interactivity through over one million manually annotated action steps from top 100 monthly active Chinese apps and tailored Android cloud real-device evaluation
methods: UItron employs a three-stage training strategy: (1) Supervised fine-tuning for GUI perception tasks including grounding, captioning, VQA, and OCR on unified multi-turn conversational data integrating multi-source datasets (e.g., Uground, Aria-UI). (2) Supervised fine-tuning for offline planning forecasting next actions from historical actions and screen observations, using distillation data from existing capable GUI agents and diverse reasoning formats with reflection mechanisms like backtracing. (3) Curriculum Reinforcement Learning (CuRL) with group relative policy optimization that first computes dense rewards from action steps in offline environments (simple), then task-level rewards in online environments (complex), with trajectory filtering by multiple VLM scoring models for reward credibility. The system is supported by an interactive infrastructure connecting both Mobile and PC devices for automatic screenshot/coordinate recording and online RL.
results: UItron achieves superior performance in benchmarks for GUI perception, grounding, and offline planning, and competitive results in online agent environments. It demonstrates substantial progress specifically in Chinese application scenarios, where even state-of-the-art solutions generally underperform. The paper notes that experimental results confirm the limitations of existing methods while showing UItron's progress toward practical real-world deployment.
limitations: The paper acknowledges that scarcity of annotated operation trajectories, limited availability of interactive infrastructure, and limited initial capabilities in foundation models remain challenges. The current version omits historical images from input to reduce computational cost, relying only on historical action information. Existing methods generally underperform in Chinese GUI scenarios, indicating a broader gap in the field.
